examples.japanese: {電報|でんぽう}を{送|おく}った。
{結婚式|けっこんしき}に{祝電|しゅくでん}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: Congratulatory telegrams arrived at the wedding.

examples.japanese: {電報|でんぽう}を{受|う}け{取|と}った。

notes:
{電報|でんぽう} refers to telegrams, which are still used in Japan for formal occasions.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {電報|でんぽう}を{送|おく}る/{打|う}つ: to send a telegram
- {電報|でんぽう}が{届|とど}く: telegram arrives
- {電報|でんぽう}を{受|う}け{取|と}る: to receive a telegram

TYPES:
- {祝電|しゅくでん}: congratulatory telegram (weddings, etc.)
- {弔電|ちょうでん}: condolence telegram (funerals)

CULTURE:
While telegrams are obsolete for everyday communication, they remain important for formal Japanese occasions. Sending a {祝電|しゅくでん} to weddings is still a common practice.

Note: NTT still offers telegram services in Japan.
